chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the earnings of the cupper, and he said, 'There is no objection to it, provided there is no conditional stipulation (sharing of risk/guarantee).'

key_terms.اَلْحَجَّامِ: The cupper (one who performs cupping therapy)
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection to it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is the income of a cupper permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the permissibility of a cupper's income is affirmed provided the transaction avoids 'musharatah', a specific conditional stipulation often interpreted in Shia jurisprudence as guaranteeing a cure or tying payment strictly to a successful outcome, which introduces uncertainty (gharar). This ruling highlights the distinction between legitimate professional service and speculative risk, a key principle in Islamic commercial law. The hadith is recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscoring its authority in deriving fiqh rulings regarding medical professions.
